evidence_items.explanation: The review reports that suggestion can elicit recollective experiences of nonexistent events, with about 15% of participants meeting its fuller-memory standard. This is relevant counterevidence to an absolute human–LLM distinction, but induced childhood memories do not measure everyday fabrication or directly contradict rarely.

TruthfulQA supplies a human–model comparison, but tests responses to questions designed around false beliefs and misconceptions. Its truthfulness scores and limited human baseline do not establish the prevalence of wholesale unintentional invention.

unresolved_gaps: No located study establishes a representative human rate of wholesale unintended factual invention on sufficiently comparable tasks.
The LLM citation study establishes a recurring failure in one task family, not its frequency across ordinary conversation.
The human false-memory studies use deliberate experimental suggestion; their rates cannot be compared directly with spontaneous model citation fabrication.
The located comparative benchmark measures a broader category of false answers than Marcus describes.
